kill_fact: No kill fact found. Every dated, load-bearing bear claim verifies against primary or licensed sources, and the two hardest ones have hardened since the record was struck: (1) BHP's own operational review for the year ended 30 June 2026 (16 July 2026) guides financial-year 2027 group copper to 1,650,000-1,800,000 tonnes against 1,952,800 tonnes delivered, with the Escondida concentrator feed grade falling from 0.90% in financial-year 2026 to about 0.70% in financial-year 2027 -- the volume trough is a filed company number, not an assertion; and (2) the Port Hedland stoppage the bear listed as a scheduled risk actually occurred and escalated (Reuters, 7 August 2026: two-day strike begins, the first major industrial action at the hub in more than two decades; Reuters, 8 August 2026: more workers joined). The one genuine defect is arithmetic, not thesis: the valuation bridge double-counts lease liabilities inside net debt, which understates all three price levels by about $1.38 per New York share. Correcting it leaves the conclusion unchanged -- at $89.98 (11 August 2026) the shares still trade about 19% above the corrected base fair value of $75.4.
corrections: 1) NET-DEBT DOUBLE COUNT (the only correction that moves a number). The record deducts 'net debt plus lease liabilities of $12.5B (company-reported net debt of about $9.0B at 30 June 2026 plus roughly $3.5B of leases)' in the base case, the same $12.5B in the favourable case, and a grossed-up $16B in the adverse case. BHP's reported net debt ALREADY INCLUDES lease liabilities -- leases sit inside Total interest bearing liabilities and, apart from a small excluded vessel/freight lease component, inside the net debt measure. Proof by reconciliation against a company-reported figure: BHP reported net debt of US$12,924m at 30 June 2025; total interest bearing liabilities of US$24,496m (of which US$2,953m lease obligations) less US$12,167m of cash and short-term investments = US$12,329m, i.e. reported net debt sits US$0.6bn above the leases-INCLUDED figure (the debt-derivative adjustment). Strip the leases out and the computed figure is US$9,376m -- US$3.5bn BELOW the company's own number, a gap no derivative adjustment explains. So the $3.5B of leases must not be added on top of the $9.0B. Removing the double count lifts every level by $3.5B / 2.5445B New York shares = $1.38: base $74.00 -> $75.38, adverse $46.00 -> $47.38, favourable $99.00 -> $100.38. Rebuilt from the record's own schedule: method 1 equity $179.0B = $70.35/sh (was $68.97), method 2 cross-check $202.8B = $79.70/sh (was $78.33), and holding the record's own position within its bracket gives a reconciled $75.4. Direction of the error runs AGAINST the bear, and it is still only 1.9% of the level -- the 19-22% premium to fair value survives untouched. 2) STALE PRICE AND RANGE ANCHOR (no valuation impact). The record is struck at $87.41 on 4 August 2026; the live quote on 11 August 2026 is $89.98, so the premium to corrected base value is 19.3% (the record's stated 18% gap understates it). The 52-week low is $51.83, not the $51.13 cited in the bear thesis and risk_reward -- the corrected adverse case of $47.4 is still below it, so the shape of the risk_reward statement holds. 3) THE ADVERSE-CASE 'INDEPENDENT' CORROBORATION IS NOT INDEPENDENT (no valuation impact). sop_bear supports its $46 typed adverse case by noting 'a published discounted cash flow analysis dated 20 July 2026 put intrinsic value at $46 against a then-price near $89.' That is a GuruFocus template DCF, and the identical $46 figure was republished on 1 June 2026 ('Intrinsic Value $46 vs Price $89'), 13 July 2026 and 20 July 2026 -- an unchanged output across seven weeks of moving inputs. It is an algorithmic constant, not a primary source or an independent valuation, and it should carry no weight. The $46 uplift over the record's own parts arithmetic of $39.22 was separately and adequately reasoned (0.7x leverage, first-quartile cost position, 50% minimum payout), so nothing numeric moves. 4) IRON ORE GUIDANCE BASIS MISMATCH (no valuation impact). The bear thesis states 'Iron ore guidance of 284-296 million tonnes is flat'. The 16 July 2026 operational review guides financial-year 2027 GROUP iron ore to 260-272 million tonnes (WAIO share 253-264Mt); 284-296Mt is WAIO on a 100% basis. The record compares that 100%-basis range against the record 265Mt shipped in financial-year 2026, which is the group/BHP-share number. The conclusion is unaffected -- 265Mt against a 260-272Mt guide is flat on a like-for-like basis -- but the two figures are not on the same basis as written. 5) THE BEAR'S NORMALISATION TRIPWIRE HAS NOT TRIGGERED, AND MOVED THE WRONG WAY (timing, not thesis). sop_bear's mechanism requires 'gold and silver by-product credits normalising so reported copper unit costs rise mechanically'. As of 11 August 2026 copper is $6.6385/lb (versus $6.65 in the record -- flat, and nowhere near the $5.80 confirming level the bear itself names), gold is $4,437.40/oz (up 6.7% from $4,157) and silver $64.92/oz (up 7.9% from $60.17). The by-product credit flattering BHP's reported copper unit costs got LARGER, not smaller, so the cost-curve reversal the bear relies on is further away than when the record was written. This does not refute the bear -- the bear states its own confirming condition and that condition is explicitly unmet -- but the adverse case is a deck-normalisation bet whose deck has since strengthened. 6) COST-CURVE AND VOLUME CLAIMS VERIFIED, NO HIDDEN DISQUALIFIER FOUND. Escondida financial-year 2026 payable copper 1,046,800t (down 7%), Spence 121,300t (down 19%), Copper South Australia 109,300t, Antamina 151,500t (up 27%); financial-year 2027 asset guidance Escondida 1,000,000-1,100,000t, Spence 210,000-230,000t, Copper South Australia 290,000-320,000t, Antamina 120,000-140,000t. Jansen Stage 2 re-budgeted to $6.9B with a $2.3B charge and first production deferred (Reuters and WSJ, 18 June 2026; shares -5.6%, worst day in fourteen months, Proactive 19 June 2026). Net debt of about $9B at 30 June 2026 confirmed. Consensus EBITDA for the year to 30 June 2027 is $29.30B (FMP consensus, 14 contributing analysts) -- the record's $29.3B anchor is exact, and the year-to-June-2026 figure of $29.86B matches its $29.9B. No undisclosed reserve downgrade, permit revocation, equity issuance or capex-funding dilution was found. On the streaming test: the $4.3B Antamina silver stream and $2B Western Australia Iron Ore power tariff are forward sales of revenue, and BHP's own framing is that together they 'unlock over US$6bn of cash' -- both sit OUTSIDE reported net debt, so the ~$9B figure understates economic leverage by an amount the bear flags qualitatively but does not quantify. I have deliberately NOT carried this into a typed correction: consensus EBITDA struck after the February 2026 announcement already reflects the forgone silver revenue, so adding it back as debt on top of the record's forward-EBITDA cross-check would double count. Flagging it as an unquantified conservatism that runs in the bear's favour.

corrections_typed.basis: BHP's reported net debt already includes lease liabilities, so the record's '$9.0B net debt + $3.5B leases = $12.5B' deduction double-counts $3.5B; proven against BHP's FY2025 Results Announcement (19 August 2025), which reports net debt of US$12,924m at 30 June 2025 versus US$24,496m total interest bearing liabilities (incl. US$2,953m leases) less US$12,167m cash and short-term investments = US$12,329m -- excluding leases would give US$9,376m, US$3.5bn below the company's own figure. Carried through the record's own schedule: method 1 equity $179.0B / 2.5445B NY shares = $70.35; method 2 cross-check ($219.8B EV less $9.0B net debt less $8B provisions) = $202.8B / 2.5445B = $79.70; holding the record's position within its own bracket gives $75.4 (a uniform +$3.5B/2.5445B = +$1.38 per share).

Same lease double count applied to the adverse schedule (19 August 2025 FY2025 Results Announcement reconciliation, as above): the record's $30B of adverse-case deductions include net debt plus leases of $16B built the same grossed-up way, so removing $3.5B gives $26.5B of deductions, equity $103.3B / 2.5445B NY shares = $40.60 versus the record's $39.22, and preserving the record's own +$6.78 uplift for the 0.7x-levered balance sheet and 50% minimum payout gives $47.4.

Same lease double count: the favourable schedule deducts the identical '$12.5B net debt plus leases', so the correct deduction is $9.0B, lifting equity from $251.4B to $254.9B and the level from $98.80 to $100.18 per New York share (rounded to the record's convention, $100.4); basis is BHP's FY2025 Results Announcement (19 August 2025) net debt reconciliation described above.

evidence: BHP, Operational review for the year ended 30 June 2026, 16 July 2026 (bhp.com/-/media/documents/media/reports-and-presentations/2026/260716_bhpoperationalreviewfortheyearended30june2026.pdf): FY2027 group copper guidance 1,650,000-1,800,000t against 1,952,800t produced in FY2026; Escondida concentrator feed grade 0.90% (FY2026) falling to about 0.70% (FY2027); Escondida FY2026 payable copper 1,046,800t (-7%), Spence 121,300t (-19%); FY2027 group iron ore guidance 260-272Mt (WAIO share 253-264Mt; WAIO 100% basis 284-296Mt) against record 265Mt in FY2026; net debt about US$9bn at 30 June 2026.

BHP FY2025 Results Announcement, 19 August 2025 (Investegate RNS 9062185; Note 21 'Net debt' of the 2025 Annual Report): reported net debt US$12,924m at 30 June 2025. Reconciled against the FY2025 balance sheet (total interest bearing liabilities US$24,496m of which US$2,953m lease obligations, less US$12,167m cash and short-term investments = US$12,329m), this is only consistent if lease liabilities are INSIDE net debt -- confirming the record's $9.0B + $3.5B = $12.5B bridge double-counts leases. Corroborated by BHP's Form 6-K net debt disclosure that, post IFRS 16, total interest bearing liabilities include all leases and only vessel lease contracts are excluded from the net debt calculation.

Reuters and WSJ, 18 June 2026 ('BHP flags cost overrun at Jansen potash project, to book $2.3 billion charge'), with Proactive Investors, 19 June 2026: Jansen Stage 2 re-budgeted to US$6.9bn, US$2.3bn write-down, first production deferred to late FY2031; Sydney shares fell 5.6%, the largest one-day drop in fourteen months. Verifies the bear's serial-project-failure leg as filed fact.

Reuters, 7 August 2026 ('Two-day strike begins at BHP's Port Hedland iron ore operations' -- the first major strike there in more than two decades) and 8 August 2026 ('More workers join strike at BHP's Port Hedland iron ore operations'), against Reuters 4 August 2026 flagging it as merely scheduled: the bear's live operational risk materialised and broadened. Live market data 11 August 2026 (FMP): BHP $89.98, 52-week range $51.83-$93.83; copper HG $6.6385/lb, gold $4,437.40/oz, silver $64.92/oz; consensus EBITDA for the year to 30 June 2027 $29.30bn across 14 analysts, matching the record's $29.3B anchor.
